'''Tengiz Beridze''' ({{langx|ka|თენგიზ გიორგის ძე ბერიძე}}; 26 October 1939 – 2 December 2024) was a Georgian biochemist.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biographical Dictionary of Georgia |url=http://www.nplg.gov.ge/bios/ka/00002462/ |publisher=National Library of the Parliament of Georgia |access-date=19 April 2022}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
In 1967 Beridze discovered [[satellite DNA]] in plants.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Beridze |first1=Thengiz |title=Satellite DNA |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-70771-1}}</ref> Through his research from 1972 to 1975, it was found that closely related species of one genus differ in satellite DNA content. In 1986 he published the monograph Satellite DNA in Springer Edition. In 2013 this monograph was edited as an eBOOK.
In 2011-17 he established a complete [[nucleotide]] sequence of four [[grape|Georgian grape]] varieties, nuclear, chloroplast and mitochondria.

In 2015–21 he established a complete [[chloroplast DNA]] sequence of Georgian wheat species.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Beridze |first1=Tengiz |title=The "Wheat Puzzle" and Kartvelians route to the Caucasus |journal=Genetic Resources and Crop Evolution |date=2019 |volume=66 |issue=4 |pages=921–927 |doi=10.1007/s10722-019-00759-9 |s2cid=254506247 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs10722-019-00759-9|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1967, he defended his Candidate's Dissertation. In 1980, he defended his doctoral dissertation in the Bakh Institute of Biochemistry, Moscow. He was elected a corresponding member of the Academy of Sciences of Georgia in 1987 and a full member in 1993.<ref>{{cite web |title=Georgian Academy of Sciences |url=http://science.org.ge/?team=tengiz-beridze&lang=en |website=Georgian Academy of Sciences |publisher=Georgian Academy of Sciences |access-date=25 December 2021}}</ref>

Beridze held various positions in Soviet and Georgian institutions since 1960s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Georgian Agrarian University |url=https://www.agruni.edu.ge/ge/t.beridze |publisher=Georgian Agrarian University}}</ref>

Beridze died on 3 December 2024, at the age of 85.<ref>[http://www.nplg.gov.ge/bios/ka/00002462/ თენგიზ ბერიძე] {{in lang|ka}}</ref>

== Positions ==
*1968–2008 – Institute of Biochemistry and Biotechnology, Georgian Academy of Sciences
*1968–1999 – Professor at Tbilisi State University, Georgia
*2008–2010 – Professor at Ilia State University, Tbilisi, Georgia
*2010–2011 – Professor at Free University of Tbilisi, Georgia 
*2012–2021 – Director of Institute of Molecular Genetics, Agricultural University of Georgia
*2012–20?? – Professor at Agricultural University of Georgia, Tbilisi, Georgia

== Awards ==
Beridze was awarded the Order of Honour of Georgia in 1999. He was awarded the Serge Durmishidze prize in Biochemistry in 2009.
